title: Yolo Wonder Bell Pepper: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics

metaDescription: Yolo Wonder bell pepper is a bell pepper variety. 90 to 110 days to harvest, 14.7 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: Yolo Wonder is a registered bell pepper variety, also sold or known as Pepper Bell Yolo Wonder. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1970. B.M. Domingo bred it. It takes 90 to 110 days from transplanting to the first harvest, with 14.67 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about Yolo Wonder bell pepper
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Yolo Wonder bell pepper takes 90 to 110 days from transplanting to the first harvest. That is about the average of the 3 bell pepper varieties with a day count, 98.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 14.67 t/ha beats the average of its group, 13.63. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives first harvest about 75 days after transplanting (Ramgo), the 1970 Seed Board row gives 90 to 110 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit bell pepper fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 14.7 t/ha in the Seed Board data.
**Fruit:** Big, thick walled fruits, green ripening to red.
**Season:** Dry season in the lowlands, all season at high elevation (Seed Board).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: on the Philippine Seed Board list since 1970, Ramgo still sells it in its professional line and garden packets. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual bell pepper on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Yolo Wonder bell pepper

Bell pepper does best in cool places such as Benguet and Bukidnon. In the lowlands, pick a heat tolerant hybrid and grow it in the dry season under some shade. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items.q: Is Pepper Bell Yolo Wonder the same as Yolo Wonder?
items.a: Yes. Pepper Bell Yolo Wonder is another name for Yolo Wonder. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 90 to 110 days from transplanting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 14.67 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Yolo Wonder?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
